hardware:
Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 2 vCPU (2 cores, 1 thread/core), 7 GiB RAM
Linux container; python 3.11.15, numpy 2.4.4, scipy-openblas 0.3.31.188.0
Benchmarks run single-threaded: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1

components.note: the ledger figure is start+complete for one cell under the advisory flock; the write figure is common.results.write_json_atomic, i.e. json encode + fsync + sha256

end_to_end.how: a real `run --fixture` of this package through common.cli, on a copy of the fixture run root with cells/ and the ledger removed; harness = wall - interpreter start-up - the summed per-cell wall_s the run recorded (which is the kernel plus the fit instrumentation)
end_to_end.includes_once_per_run_costs: the matrix write, protocol snapshot, code provenance and the interrupted sweep happen once per run and are amortised over 12 fixture cells here, so this per-cell figure OVERSTATES the production one

harness.how: end-to-end harness seconds per cell measured on the fixture, with the scale-dependent components (ledger length, result-file bytes) swapped from the fixture scale to the production scale: 0.0047382 - 0.0018072 + 0.0019217 = 0.0048526
harness.per_worker_note: the interpreter start-up and package import above is paid once per worker PROCESS, not once per cell; a scheduler that starts a fresh process per cell pays it on every cell instead, which would add 0.1141 s x 136 cells = 15.52 CPU-s
harness.serial_note: ledger start+complete run under an advisory flock on one lock file, so they do not parallelise: this is a floor on the wall time that no worker count beats

deterministic_cell.call_path: t19s.runner.run_deterministic_cell on the G1 population operator (8 eps points, one eigen solve each)

exponent_check.note: the measured exponent is BELOW the algorithm's by 1.22: at these sizes the kernel is not yet flop-bound (Python/allocation overhead dominates), so a projection made with the fitted exponent UNDERSTATES the cost at larger sizes and one made with the theoretical exponent overstates it at these ones

deterministic_cell.notes: every d = 256 deterministic/control family runs this same code path with a different direction

memory.rss_is: VmHWM of THIS process (resident high-water mark, never decreases); meaningful per size only when measured in a fresh subprocess
memory.ru_maxrss_is: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss, which Linux INHERITS across fork: in a process spawned by a benchmark driver it is at least the driver's own high-water mark and says nothing about this call.  Kept for the record; rss_high_water_bytes is the one to read
memory.tracemalloc_is: peak Python-allocator bytes for this call only

theory.note: eigendecomposition of a d x d matrix is O(d^3)

paired_cell.call_path: t19s.synthetic.run_paired_cell (32 cw_pca fits + 29 eigen solves per cell; the m/d = 2048 noise-only calibration stream of 2048*d rows dominates)

exponent_check.note: the measured exponent is BELOW the algorithm's by 0.93: at these sizes the kernel is not yet flop-bound (Python/allocation overhead dominates), so a projection made with the fitted exponent UNDERSTATES the cost at larger sizes and one made with the theoretical exponent overstates it at these ones

paired_cell.notes: N is held at the production aspect ratio N = 2d so the d = 256 point IS one production paired cell

notes: The production paired cell (d = 256, N = 512) is inside the benchmarked range, so the paired projection is a MEASUREMENT, not an extrapolation.
Within one paired cell the cost is dominated by the m/d = 2048 calibration stream (2048 d rows accumulated as Z^T Z, i.e. O(2048 d^3)), not by the 32 CW-PCA fits.

reduce.bound_note: reduce reads every cell file once; measured throughput 0.5 MB/s over 12 cells (0.32 MB of input) against a warm page cache, so the step is compute-bound AT THAT SIZE.  This is not a claim about the production scale; see reduction_work.at_production_scale in RESOURCE_ESTIMATE.json

requirements.pip_dry_run_note: a real `pip install` of these pins was NOT timed: this container already satisfies them and has no guaranteed network egress, so the honest figure is the check time above. On a remote host without them, budget the download of numpy+scipy wheels (~90 MB) plus install, which is link-dependent and UNKNOWN.

transfer.note: the wall time of the transfer depends on the link, which is UNKNOWN; only the size is a fact. Measured on a build of this handoff; successive builds differ by a few tens of kB (timestamps, this report and the estimate files) - two builds of the same tree measured here were 7 702 123 and 7 764 484 bytes.
